update.headline: Risk appetite improved on the day as yields fell, but the macro mix stayed stagflationary: headline inflation re-accelerated, labor softened, and market leadership remained narrow in technology.
update.economy: Inflation was mixed but not benign. CPI y/y rose to 3.71%, up 0.17 pp, and CPI m/m rose to 0.4%, up 0.33 pp. PCE y/y rose to 3.42%, up 0.06 pp, and PCE m/m rose to 0.31%, up 0.26 pp. Core CPI y/y eased to 2.76%, down -0.03 pp, but core CPI m/m firmed to 0.29%, up 0.07 pp; core PCE y/y rose to 3.01%, up 0.03 pp, and core PCE m/m rose to 0.25%, up 0.12 pp. Labor cooled at the margin: unemployment rose to 4.2%, up 0.1 pp, while payrolls y/y slowed to 0.31%, down -0.03 pp. Industrial production y/y improved to 1.42%, up 0.29 pp. Consensus and surprise data are unavailable for the releases. Data gaps: none. Model note: none.
update.asset_classes: Equities rallied on the daily rates reprieve: SPY gained 0.74%, QQQ gained 1.02%, and XLK gained 1.01%. That fits the running theme of narrow technology leadership: QQQ is up 5.8% over 1 month and XLK is up 8.96% over 1 month, while XLF is down -6.9%, XLY is down -3.99%, XLV is down -3.55%, and XLI is down -1.37%. Rates softened on the day, with DGS2 down -10.0 bp and DGS10 down -5.0 bp, helping growth equities, but the 1-month move still shows duration pressure: DGS2 is up 39.0 bp and DGS10 is up 45.0 bp, while TLT is down -5.07%, IEF is down -3.06%, and LQD is down -2.92% over 1 month. Credit was mixed on the day, with LQD down -0.2% and HYG up 0.01%, but both remain weaker over 1 month. Commodities were uneven: oil weakened on the day, with USO down -1.77% and CL_F down -1.54%, while gold signals diverged, with GLD down -0.68% and GC_F up 0.59%. FX still shows stronger-dollar stress over 1 month: EURUSD is down -3.64%, AUDUSD is down -3.39%, GBPUSD is down -2.26%, and USDCAD is up 2.71%, though AUDUSD gained 0.42% and GBPUSD gained 0.2% on the day.
update.predictions_changed: No regime prediction changed. The growth model gate was unchanged, so the old and new prediction were kept the same; this should be read as no forecast change, not as a fresh refit signal. The inflation model gate was also unchanged, so its prediction was kept the same for the same reason.

themes_touched.title: Narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness
themes_touched.text: Still active. The day was risk-on, but leadership stayed concentrated in technology: QQQ rose 1.02% and XLK rose 1.01%, ahead of SPY at 0.74%. Over 1 month, XLK is up 8.96% and QQQ is up 5.8%, while XLF is down -6.9%, XLY is down -3.99%, XLV is down -3.55%, and XLI is down -1.37%. This remains narrow leadership rather than broad cyclical confirmation.

themes_touched.title: Duration pressure and stronger-dollar stress
themes_touched.text: Still active, despite the daily yield rally. DGS2 fell -10.0 bp and DGS10 fell -5.0 bp on the day, which supported growth equities, but over 1 month DGS2 is up 39.0 bp and DGS10 is up 45.0 bp. Duration-sensitive assets remain under pressure over 1 month, with TLT down -5.07%, IEF down -3.06%, LQD down -2.92%, and GLD down -5.62%. The dollar backdrop also remains firm over 1 month, with EURUSD down -3.64%, AUDUSD down -3.39%, GBPUSD down -2.26%, and USDCAD up 2.71%.

sector_reads.text: Energy is still a short-term pullback inside a strong long-term uptrend, not a reversal. XLE is up 1.26% over 1 week but down -2.93% over 1 month, with -3.77 pp relative 1-month performance. The long trend remains strong: 18.94% over 3 months, 7.42% over 6 months, 44.64% over 12 months, and 28.26 pp relative 12-month performance. Oil weakness, with USO down -1.77% and CL_F down -1.54% on the day, explains the near-term drag.

Financials remain weak and look more like downside within a range than a pullback in leadership. XLF is down -2.46% over 1 week, -6.9% over 1 month, and -4.38% over 3 months, with -7.74 pp relative 1-month performance. The 12-month return is only 1.77%, and relative 12-month performance is -14.61 pp, consistent with a range-bound long trend and continuing underperformance.

Industrials are in a short-term pullback within a fading longer uptrend. XLI is down -0.28% over 1 week, -1.37% over 1 month, and -8.17% over 3 months, with -2.21 pp relative 1-month performance. It remains up 4.31% over 6 months and 11.76% over 12 months, but relative 12-month performance is -4.62 pp. That argues pullback rather than confirmed reversal, though trend quality is fading.

Health care’s short-term weakness has deepened, but it still looks like a correction within a longer uptrend. XLV is down -2.65% over 1 week and -3.55% over 1 month, with -4.39 pp relative 1-month performance. Longer-term returns remain positive at 3.0% over 3 months, 14.13% over 6 months, and 17.76% over 12 months, with 1.38 pp relative 12-month performance.

Technology remains the clear leadership sector. XLK is up 1.8% over 1 week, 8.96% over 1 month, 8.97% over 3 months, 47.28% over 6 months, and 41.12% over 12 months, with 8.12 pp relative 1-month performance and 24.74 pp relative 12-month performance. The short label is up, fading, so momentum may be moderating, but this still looks like leadership, not reversal.

Consumer discretionary weakness remains a continuation of a downtrend, not a simple pullback. XLY is down -0.47% over 1 week, -3.99% over 1 month, and -6.55% over 3 months, with -4.83 pp relative 1-month performance. The long trend is also weak: XLY is down -7.98% over 12 months, with -24.36 pp relative 12-month performance. The 1.13% daily gain looks like a bounce within a downtrend rather than a reversal.
